how_to_apply: Visit the official website opsc.gov.in and carefully read the full advertisement before filling the online application.
Register and complete the automated, system-driven online application form; ensure all information entered is accurate before submission.
Upload a scanned passport-size photograph (unsigned and unattested, within the last 6 months), scanned full signature, and scanned Left-Hand Thumb Impression (LTI), all clearly identifiable.
Pay the examination fee of ₹700 online (except SC/ST/PwD candidates, who are exempted).
Upload all required certificates and documents in original scanned form via the Commission's e-Chayan portal.
On successful submission, a unique Permanent Public Service Account Number (PPSAN) will be assigned.
Verify the submitted copy of the application; to modify any information, cancel and reapply within the last date.
Take a printout of the finally submitted registration and application form, sign the declaration, and retain it along with copies of the required certificates for verification when asked.
Download the Admission Certificate from the OPSC website before the written exam date and carry it to the examination centre.

content_sections.heading: OPSC AAE Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: A candidate must hold a Bachelor's Degree in Agriculture Engineering from any University or Institution recognised by any State Government or the Government of India. No other equivalent qualification except a Degree in Agriculture Engineering will be accepted. Candidates must be able to read, write and speak Odia, and must satisfy at least one of the following: Passed Middle School Examination with Odia as a language subject; or Passed Matriculation or an equivalent examination with Odia as the medium of examination in a non-language subject; or Passed Odia as a language subject in the final examination of Class VII from a School or Educational Institution recognised by the Government of Odisha or the Central Government; or Passed a test in Odia at Middle English School Standard, conducted by the School & Mass Education Department, Government of Odisha, or the Board of Secondary Education, Odisha. Must be a citizen of India. Must be of sound mental condition and bodily health, free from any physical or mental defect likely to interfere with the discharge of duties (this provision does not apply to physically handicapped candidates); every selected candidate will be examined by a Medical Board. A candidate with more than one living spouse is not eligible unless exempted by the State Government for good and sufficient reasons. Serving Government servants (temporary or permanent) are eligible if they meet the age and qualification criteria, but must inform their Head of Office in writing and furnish a No Objection Certificate at the time of document verification. Candidates debarred by OPSC, another State PSC, or UPSC from appearing in any examination/interview for a specific period are not eligible to apply during that period.

content_sections.heading: Examination Fee
content_sections.text: Note: The examination fee is refunded only to candidates who actually appear in both papers of the Written Examination, processed to the original mode of payment after the exam. Applications without fee payment (except for SC/ST/PwD) will be treated as incomplete and rejected outright. Candidates must furnish accurate bank account details (account number, IFSC code, account holder name, bank branch) in case the original-mode refund fails.

content_sections.heading: OPSC AAE Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection is through a competitive examination comprising a Written Examination followed by a Personality Test (Interview). Both papers are Objective Type (MCQ) with OMR-based evaluation; each question carries 1 mark. Negative marking: 25% of the marks allotted to a question is deducted for each wrong answer; unattempted questions receive zero marks. The Commission will fix qualifying marks for each paper and/or in aggregate, category-wise. Candidates meeting the qualifying marks are shortlisted for the Personality Test in a ratio of about 1:2 of the advertised vacancies (category-wise), subject to a minimum of 5 candidates per category. Carries 25 marks . The Select List is drawn in order of merit based on aggregate marks (Written Examination + Interview, out of 225) for each category, equal to the number of advertised vacancies. Ties are resolved first by Written Examination marks, and if still tied, the older candidate is placed higher.

content_sections.heading: OPSC AAE Syllabus Highlights
content_sections.text: The syllabus is at Bachelor's Degree standard. Key topics include: Paper-I, Section A (General Engineering): Computer programming & data structures, workshop practice, applied electronics & instrumentation, common statistical data on agriculture, units & dimensions, surveying & levelling, building construction & cost estimation, greenhouse design. Paper-I, Section B (Farm Machinery & Power): Farm machinery, farm power, tractor systems & controls, farm power/machinery management, human engineering & safety, precision agriculture, renewable energy engineering, systems engineering. Paper-II, Section A (Agricultural Processing & Food Engineering): Engineering properties of food materials, grain processing, drying & storage of crops, horticultural produce processing, thermal processing, food laws (FSSAI, BIS, Codex). Paper-II, Section B (Soil & Water Conservation Engineering): Fluid mechanics, irrigation engineering, drainage engineering, groundwater/wells/pumps, hydrology, soil & water conservation engineering and watershed management. The full detailed syllabus is published as Appendix-A of the official notification.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for OPSC AAE Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Important: Applications received through any mode other than the OPSC online portal will not be accepted and will be summarily rejected. Do not attach original certificates to the application — only self-attested copies are required at the document verification stage, marked "Submitted by me and Certified as genuine and has not been cancelled" with full signature and date.

content_sections.heading: Documents Required
content_sections.text: HSC or equivalent certificate (proof of date of birth) Intermediate/+2 examination certificate Bachelor's Degree in Agriculture Engineering certificate from a recognised University/Institution Mark sheets for all examinations from HSC to the Bachelor's Degree (including any failed attempts, if applicable) Four recent passport-size photographs (unsigned and unattested, within 6 months) Caste certificate in support of SEBC/SC/ST claim, where applicable (SEBC certificate must be issued on or after 29 August 2023) Odia Test Pass certificate, or equivalent certificate as specified in the eligibility conditions Permanent Disability Certificate (40% or more) from the concerned Medical Board, where applicable Release Certificate for Ex-Servicemen, along with a notarised Affidavit (format at Appendix-B) No Objection Certificate from the Competent Authority/Head of Office, where applicable Proof of identity (Aadhaar/EPIC/Driving Licence/Passport/PAN Card) Identity Certificate/Card for Third Gender/Transgender candidates, where applicable

faq.question: Q1. How many Assistant Agriculture Engineer posts are available?
faq.answer: OPSC has notified 48 (16-w) posts of Assistant Agriculture Engineer under Advertisement No. 08 of 2026-27.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply?
faq.answer: Online applications close on 28 September 2026 at 5:00 PM. The link opens on 28 August 2026.

faq.question: Q3. What is the age limit for OPSC AAE?
faq.answer: Candidates must be between 21 and 42 years as on 1 January 2026, subject to applicable relaxation for SEBC/SC/ST/Women/Ex-Servicemen/PwD candidates.

faq.question: Q4. What is the educational qualification required?
faq.answer: A Bachelor's Degree in Agriculture Engineering from a recognised University or Institution; no other equivalent qualification is accepted.

faq.question: Q5. Is knowledge of Odia mandatory?
faq.answer: Yes. Candidates must be able to read, write and speak Odia, and must meet one of the specified Odia-qualification conditions (Middle School Odia, Matriculation with Odia medium, Class VII Odia, or an Odia test pass).

faq.question: Q6. What is the pay scale?
faq.answer: Starting basic pay of ₹44,900 per month at Level-10, Cell-1 of the Pay Matrix under ORSP Rules, 2017, plus usual allowances.

faq.question: Q7. When is the written examination?
faq.answer: The Written Examination is scheduled for 1 November 2026 (Sunday), at centres in Cuttack/Bhubaneswar.

faq.question: Q8. What is the exam fee and is it refundable?
faq.answer: ₹700 for candidates other than SC/ST/PwD, refunded only to those who appear in both papers of the Written Examination.
